site.text002: I'm Giselly Pereira, I'm 24 years old and I live in São Luís, Maranhão, Brazil.
site.text003: I'm curious, I enjoy learning new things and creating. Programming gave me a space to put my ideas and creativity into practice.
site.text005: Giselly wearing a pink T-shirt beside a bookshelf.
site.text009: In 2020, I started studying nursing. In my fourth semester, I put my degree on hold to study programming, encouraged by my brother, who already worked in the field.
site.text010: It was a challenge because I barely knew how to use a computer. There were many courses and lessons, and people in the field helped me figure out where to start.
site.text011: I worked hard and gradually found my way. What I enjoy most is bringing my ideas and creativity into my work.
site.text012: This portfolio reflects that. While building it, I wanted it to show a little of who I am, even in the smallest details.

site.text062: I was responsible for the complete front-end development of the school management system for Escola Caminho das Estrelas, affiliated with the Brazilian Air Force (FAB). I implemented the interfaces in React, Next.js and TypeScript and integrated the workflows with the API, collaborating with the back-end team and taking part in testing. My work also included UI/UX design: shaping the experience and turning it into an application connected to the system's data and business rules.
site.text063: FAB school management system login screen, with a child astronaut in a rocket
site.text064: The starting point was a school that handled enrollment, attendance and grades entirely by hand. The complexity lay in bringing those routines into a platform for multiple institutions and campuses, with specific workflows for super administrators, administrators, teachers, students and parents or guardians. On the front end, this meant translating institutional rules into navigation and user workflows, aligning screen behavior with back-end integrations and testing.
site.text065: I delivered responsive front-end workflows for enrollment, attendance records, grade entry and communication with guardians. The system was demonstrated at an educational event at the Alcântara Launch Center (CLA), leading to a partnership with the school for the testing phase. The school now accesses it through a VPN, restricted to the base's internal environment. The project brought my interface work into a real institutional setting, with cross-team collaboration, data integration and validation alongside the school.
site.text066: I worked on the Teatro Arthur Azevedo website in partnership with the theater's coordination and design team. The project presents the history of the cultural venue and Arthur Azevedo's life, connecting heritage, collections and events in a digital experience. My work combined interface implementation, content management integration, animations and interactions, translating the visual concept into navigation that balances the institution's classical character with an engaging, playful experience.
site.text067: Teatro Arthur Azevedo homepage with an illustration of its historic facade
site.text069: The challenge was to turn diverse content — history, news, collections, galleries and a cultural calendar — into clear paths for discovery and reference. Working with the design team, I balanced the theater's classical identity with interactive elements that spark visitors' curiosity. The content management integration also needed to reflect updates from the responsible team, organizing photos by category and event information while keeping the experience cohesive.
site.text070: I delivered a responsive interface integrated with the system that supplies news, digital collections, information about physical collections and photo galleries organized by category. The calendar brings together cultural events, with descriptions, dates and times, plus access to online ticketing. Animations and interactions connect the content to the project's identity and make exploration more engaging. The solution lets the team keep information up to date independently and brings the public closer to the venue's history and activities.
site.text071: I worked with the design team on the Museu do Palácio dos Leões website to present the historical and cultural richness of one of Maranhão's major heritage sites. The project brings together the palace's history, collections, galleries and the state's governors. My work connected interface implementation with content management integration, translating the visual direction into a responsive experience with a classical, traditional style that respects the venue's institutional and museum character.
site.text072: Museu do Palácio dos Leões homepage with a photograph of its historic rooms
site.text073: The challenge was to organize a large amount of historical and cultural information into clear navigation, preserving the context of each item and the palace's classical identity. This included presenting Maranhão's governors from the imperial and republican periods to the current administration, along with the museum's collections and galleries. The experience also needed to work across screen sizes and offer content in six languages, keeping the information consistent for Brazilian and international audiences.
site.text074: I delivered a responsive website integrated with the content management system, enabling the museum team to add and update content. The platform brings together the history of Palácio dos Leões, collection information, galleries and records of Maranhão's governors, organized by historical period. Content is available in Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, Japanese and Mandarin Chinese, widening access to this cultural heritage. The solution combines editorial independence with a classical presentation and navigation that encourages exploration of a rich collection.
site.text075: I created Libris as a personal project to explore animation, creativity and user experience in a digital library integrated with the Google Books API. I was responsible for the layout, the complete front end, and unit and integration tests. The concept brings the interface closer to the world of reading: saved books appear on a bookshelf, making collection organization part of the visual experience. Built with React and TypeScript, the project combines its own identity with book and magazine discovery, interactions and reading tracking.
site.text076: Book discovery screen in the Libris personal library
site.text077: The challenge was to turn a broad catalog of books and magazines into a distinctive discovery and organization experience while keeping it clear and fluid. Alongside the layout and animations, I worked on search, filters, loading, error and empty states. I separated remote API data, managed with TanStack Query, from bookshelf state, persisted in the browser with Zustand. I also balanced the shelf presentation with a table view, adapting navigation for mobile devices and respecting reduced-motion preferences.
site.text078: I delivered a responsive application with search by title, author or subject, reading suggestions, magazine browsing and book details, including previews when available. Users can save and remove titles, track Want to read, Reading and Read statuses, and organize their collection with search, filters, sorting and pagination. Light and dark themes and animations reinforce the product's identity. I implemented Vitest and React Testing Library tests for components, integrations and user workflows, covering the full front-end project cycle: visual concept, implementation, API integration and behavior validation.

site.text094: Improving the app meant balancing user experience changes with the rules and limitations of the previous solution. In Figma, I redesigned and adapted the workflows within what could be changed; during implementation, I rebuilt the app in React Native and connected the journeys to the necessary integrations. The focus was to make access to services clearer while preserving the continuity of existing public services.
site.text095: The new version expanded access to appointments and service notifications, integrated news and verification of ID cards for people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). It also added a complaints workflow, allowing residents to submit requests directly through the app. Available on Android and iOS, Viva Procon brings these services together in a mobile experience serving the entire state.

site.text107: The challenge was to turn a broad editorial concept into a mobile experience that is easy to explore. I worked on category organization, news hierarchy and reading workflows to make different topics and formats clear. The context also required understanding how AI agents supplied the product — from image generation to news production and publication — and taking that process into account in interface decisions.
site.text108: I developed the front end for the new experience, with topic navigation, favorites and reading preferences, in an app published on the App Store. Alongside AI-generated news and images, HubNews offers podcasts featuring conversations between artificial intelligences, providing more ways to access content. The project deepened my experience of moving from idea to implementation and my understanding of products powered by AI agents, connecting interface design, mobile development and content distribution.

I developed institutional and cultural apps and websites for the Maranhão government with the systems team: React Native, Expo, TypeScript and JavaScript for mobile; React and responsive web interfaces integrated with content management for history, collections, galleries and events. I implemented REST APIs, authentication, forms with Yup and image uploads.

On mobile, I worked with Expo Router and React Navigation; Firebase FCM and Expo Notifications push notifications in foreground, background and with the app closed; notification history and read status in SQLite; AsyncStorage persistence; camera, gallery, WebView and vibration, managing permissions on Android and iOS.

I configured Expo SDK, native modules, and development, preview and production profiles in EAS Build, with APK, AAB and automatic version increments. I organized reusable components and optimized rendering and lists with memoization, FlatList and on-demand loading. I took part in code reviews and Git version control and was responsible for publishing and updating apps on the App Store and Google Play.
site.text142:
I was one of the developers responsible for store interfaces for Nike, Chilli Beans, Authentic Feet, Santa Lolla, Móveis Linhares, Vivavinhos, Nautika and Artwalk. I implemented and maintained these e-commerce websites in VTEX CMS and VTEX IO. I worked directly with clients through Monday to receive requests, clarify needs and align each request's features and resources.

In VTEX CMS, I built and adjusted page structure with HTML, styling with CSS and Sass, and interactions with JavaScript. In VTEX IO, I implemented React components and composed them within store interfaces. I implemented layouts supplied by clients or created by the design team, preserving each brand's visual identity.
site.text145: Systems for notarial and civil registry offices
site.text146:
I developed the front end of three systems for notarial and civil registry offices as a mid-level developer, participating in requirements analysis, screen implementation and maintenance. I worked on civil registration workflows — births, deaths and marriages — and services for deeds, document authentication and formal debt protests. I implemented data entry, record lookup and information interfaces, including data exchange between offices, collaborating with other teams.

I used React, Vite and JavaScript, Redux for state management and Tailwind CSS for styling. I built forms with Formik, date selection with Datepicker and icons with React Icons. I was responsible for back-end integration, connecting forms and queries to the system's services and displaying returned data. I also worked on environment configuration with Docker and MySQL 8.
site.text149:
I worked with the team on a church management system and its companion app. On the web front end, I implemented React screens and components from the team's layouts, using Redux for state management, Tailwind CSS and Material UI for interfaces, and integrating screens with APIs. On mobile, I contributed to the React Native app.

I developed financial features for recording and tracking cash inflows and outflows, member registration and management, and birthday lists. My work involved turning administrative routines into functional screens, connecting system data to interfaces, fixing bugs and proposing improvements with the team. I also took part in code review, organization and adjustments needed for delivery.
site.text152: From web to mobile, every team and project has broadened the way I think, create and develop. These are the chapters of that journey.
site.text153: And I'm still writing the next chapters.
